messages:
maria: incident-bot fired: repeated CUDA_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS events on pool/gpu-shard-7 at 03:17 UTC. Error spike shows ~15% failing generations. Noticing container restarts. Paging oncall.

incident-bot: Paging alert -> @ryan-sre (primary), @julia-ml (backup). Incident tag INC-215000. Autoscaler paused for affected shard.

oncall-bot: Reminder to include severity and customer impact in first update.

ryan-sre: I'm on. Quick read: 502/503 uptick for /v1/generate. Which model variants?

maria: redwood/gen-large and redwood/gen-large-quant both saw failures. Root crashes show illegal access in attention kernel after large decode batches.

julia-ml: Snippet from driver:
```
E Runtime: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS @ attention_kernel.cu:1190
ctx: multistream decode, kv_cache write after page fault
batch=48, seq=1536
```
Hypothesis: race when KV cache maps/unmaps across threads during refill.

ryan-sre: Runbook: cordon + drain affected node(s), collect nvcrash and core dumps, fallback routing to CPU variant, lower batch_size, toggle safe-mmap flag on runtime.

infra-bot: Cordon initiated for gpu-shard-7. Draining with PDB awareness. ETA ~90s.

kevin-platform: If we route to CPU fallback, expect ~2x latency and cost spike. Recommend throttled rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% for highest priority tenants.

maria: Applying runtime flag: runtime.kv_refill.serialize=true on service redwood/gen-large to force single-thread refill.

ops-bot: Config change applied by maria: runtime.kv_refill.serialize -> true

julia-ml: Also recommend lowering default batch size to 12 for redwood/gen-large. This reduces concurrency on the kernel path.

ryan-sre: Applying batch_size change now via config API.

ops-bot: batch_size set to 12 for redwood/gen-large (change agent: ryan-sre)

maria: Deploying CPU fallback route for top-tier tenants at 5%.

kevin-platform: Reroute policy in place. Watchless: spillover may affect Dedicated pool capacity.

ryan-sre: Drain complete for gpu-shard-7. Observed 6 pod restarts before graceful exit. Node tainted quarantined. Collecting core.

maria: Command used to pull core:
```
kubectl cp pod-gen-7:/tmp/core.dump ./core.7.dmp
aws s3 cp ./core.7.dmp s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-215000/
```

julia-ml: Reproducer run in staging: seq_len=1536, batch=48, streams=6 causes same illegal address after ~10 minutes. With serialize=true, no crash observed in 30m.

ryan-sre: Good. Immediate mitigations seem effective: error rate down from 15% -> 3%. CPU fallback added tail-latency ~180ms for affected requests.

maria: Customer comms draft: "We're investigating GPU runtime errors causing intermittent timeouts on generation endpoints. Traffic is temporarily routed to fallback compute and batch sizes have been reduced. Engineers are collecting logs and will provide updates every 30 minutes." Approve? @cust-ops

cust-ops: Approve. Add note about potential cost increase and SLA impact window.

kevin-platform: File upstream driver report with collected stack and nvcrash. Ticket created: DRV-3157.

ryan-sre: Next: prepare hotpatch to enforce serialization on KV refill and consider micro-rollback window to older runtime where the mapping behavior differed. Schedule postmortem once stabilized.

sre-rotation: Acknowledged handoff in 40m. Will take over if mitigations remain active.

incident-bot: Incident INC-215000 status: mitigated -> partial. Severity: Sev2. Artifacts: core dump, nvcrash, staging reproducer logs.

maria: Plan for next update in 30 minutes. If anyone sees new 5xx noise, signal ASAP. Closing loop: suspected kernel race during concurrent KV cache pagewalk/unmap causing illegal address. Temporary mitigations: node quarantine, batch reduction, serialize KV refill flag, CPU fallback. Permanent: driver/kernel patch or runtime-level serialization and further QA.
